Subject: ACME: Private deploy cutover — readiness confirmation & network test window

Hi Aditya / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the prep — quick check from Acme EdgeOps before we sign the window. We plan to run the final brown‑field cut (private deployment into our colo VPC) on the evening window: 2027‑06‑21 02:00–04:00 UTC. Can you confirm the following by EOD Friday: 

- That your runbook version 1.3 (attached) is the canonical copy we should follow.
- Expected KV cache priming duration and whether there are any persistent prefix warmup steps we should run from our side.
- Whether the network team should expect any BGP withdraws or route‑refresh chatter during the 5m test bursts.
- A short list of playbook rollback triggers (we have our change board that will watch these).

We have a small set of test flows we can run from the colo (sample pings/trace, small synthetic inference requests) — if you can confirm the health checks that should pass for a clean handback, that’ll help.

Attaching ACME_Runbook_v1.3.pdf and our postcutover checklist template.

Appreciate a concise confirmation (yes/no + short notes) — CJ

--
Clara Jensen
EdgeOps — Acme Retail
edge-ops@acmeretail.com

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ACME: Private deploy cutover — readiness confirmation & network test window

Thanks Clara — confirmable items below. Short answers first, details after:

- Canonical runbook: yes, ACME_Runbook_v1.3.pdf is the canonical runbook we will use.
- KV priming: expect 8–12 minutes for a full prefix warmup for the 4k‑token profile; full KV cache steady state ~25m if you exercise end‑to‑end inference traffic.
- BGP activity: we will not withdraw prefixes intentionally; the only expected control‑plane chatter will be transient ARP/ND and an internal route‑refresh during test fluidity.
- Rollback triggers (brief): token path errors >3% within 5 minutes, persistent 5xx rates on inference API, inability to establish TLS to the private node for >2m.

Monica — can you confirm the priming script and attach the warmup log template? Marissa — please confirm Ops bridge time and who will own paging for first‑hour escalations.

I’m attaching our postcutover checklist (postcutover-checklist.csv) and a short preflight script. We’ll be on the bridge 01:30 UTC for a quick alignment.

Quick status update from infra priming side: 

- Warmup script (warmup_v2.sh) executed in our staging fabric this morning; attached priming-log.txt is a condensed run from a 10m warmup showing steady KV hit rates at ~92% after 12 minutes.
- We detected an MTU mismatch on the north‑sider transit fabric (1500 vs 9000) between one TOR and the customer router during a mirror run; that was adjusted on the TOR and we revalidated — no packet drops seen now.
- Health checks we expect to pass during the window: TLS handshake (port 443), /healthz API returning 200 with green state, sample inference vector against model v3.1 returning JSON within 450ms p50 for the synthetic microflow.

Attachments: priming-log.txt (excerpt), interface-acls.json (snippet).

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0400
Subject: Final playbacks and go/no‑go inputs — ACME private cutover (21 Jun)

Clara / EdgeOps,

We ran the planned preflight playback at 13:00 UTC and exercised the following items against the staging colo mirror: 

1) KV cache priming: PASS — steady state 92–95% hit rate after 14m (see priming-log.txt).
2) Network stability: PASS — MTU mismatch found and corrected; no BGP withdraws observed.
3) TLS + health: PASS — all nodes responded with /healthz=200 and TLS ciphers negotiated correctly.
4) Synthetic microflow latency: WARN -> observed p95 780ms on the largest payload; p50 ~420ms. We recommend limiting the initial traffic ramp for the first 15 minutes to the smallest payloads, then step to normal traffic at +30m once KV steady state is confirmed.
5) Rollback triggers validated: the automated pager will fire on 5xx burst >3% or TLS failures >2m.

Summary recommendation: GREEN for cutover with a controlled ramp plan. Suggested 0–15m: synthetic tiny traffic only; 15–45m: mixed traffic; 45m+: full traffic if KV steady state maintained and no >3xx error spikes.

Next steps:
- I’ll upload the final postcutover-checklist.csv (filled) to the drive link and sign the DocuSign acknowledgement.
- Marissa — please confirm bridge owner and escalation matrix.

Thanks all — looking forward to a smooth window.
